headline: Data center demand drives a sharp profit turnaround
summary_short: Revenue rose 42.2% y/y to $170.9M on strong Compute and Communications demand, while operating income swung to $26.1M from $7.0M a year ago as gross margin expanded 80bp to 68.0%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 42.2% y/y to $170.9M, led by an 86% surge in Compute and Communications (data center, AI-specific and general-purpose servers, plus wireline networking) and 2% growth in Industrial and Embedded on recovering industrial/aerospace demand. Gross margin rose 80bp to 68.0% on favorable product mix and volume, partly offset by higher stock-based compensation. Operating income reached $26.1M versus $7.0M a year ago. Net income was $21.8M ($0.16 diluted EPS) versus $5.0M ($0.04) a year ago. Operating cash flow rose to $50.3M from $31.9M. Cash and equivalents were $140.0M; the company repurchased $15.0M of stock under its $250M program. No forward guidance was given in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth accelerated to 42% y/y led by data center and AI-related demand in Compute and Communications, driving a sharp swing to profitability in operating income, net income, and cash generation.

Compute and Communications revenue rose 86% y/y on stronger data center demand (general-purpose and AI-specific servers) plus wireline networking; Industrial and Embedded rose 2% on recovering industrial/aerospace demand.
Gross margin rose 80bp y/y to 68.0% on favorable product mix and volume, partially offset by higher stock-based compensation tied to market- and performance-based awards.
Operating income rose to $26.1M from $7.0M as revenue growth and 80bp of gross-margin expansion outpaced opex growth, which was driven by higher stock-based compensation.
EBIT is a Yahoo-derived figure, not a line the 10-Q discloses directly; it moved with GAAP operating income for the same reasons (revenue growth, margin expansion).

This KPI is Yahoo's own EBITDA calculation. The filing separately discloses its own non-GAAP 'Adjusted EBITDA' of $67.8M (39.6% margin), up from $40.1M, driven by higher revenue partly offset by higher headcount costs — the two figures are not directly comparable.
Net income rose to $21.8M from $5.0M on higher operating income, partly offset by higher income tax expense ($5.4M vs $3.0M) from increased worldwide income and stock-compensation effects.
EPS grew roughly in step with net income; diluted share count was little changed y/y (139.4M vs 138.3M).
EPS grew roughly in step with net income; basic share count was little changed y/y.
Cash from operations rose to $50.3M from $31.9M as $27.6M of higher net-income-adjusted-for-non-cash-items was partly offset by $9.2M of net working-capital changes.
